content:
Optimizing your AI stack for a customer you don't have yet is premature compliance theater.

PG said it plainly: use what ships the best product. Full stop.

---

The founders sweating Anthropic's DoD policy at pre-seed are solving a Series C problem. That's not prudence — that's procrastination dressed up as strategy.

---

Build the thing. Win the customer. Then negotiate the compliance requirements from a position of leverage.

Vendor risk is real. But irrelevance kills faster.

What's the biggest vendor decision you've overthought early that didn't matter once you had traction?
source_story_title: Paul Graham Endorses Anthropic for Early-Stage Startups Despite DoD Concerns
source_story_summary: Paul Graham publicly advised early-stage founders not to avoid Anthropic's AI models simply because of concerns about potential future DoD sales restrictions. He argued that at the early stage, product quality is paramount, and if Anthropic delivers the best results, founders should use it without overthinking future enterprise compliance constraints.

content:
The most powerful crisis move isn't a PR statement. It's an AMA.

Anthropic's CEO sat in public heat over the DoD partnership and said: ask me anything. That's not spin. That's conviction.

---

Founders take note: silence reads as guilt. Transparency reads as leadership. The companies that will own foundational AI infrastructure are the ones that can hold scrutiny without flinching.

---

If you're building on Anthropic's stack, this week should increase your confidence, not shake it. A CEO who answers hard questions live is one you can build on.

Trust is infrastructure too. Agree or disagree?
source_story_title: Anthropic CEO Conducts Live AMA on DoD Partnership Amid Controversy
source_story_summary: Anthropic's CEO publicly offered to answer questions about the company's work with the Department of Defense and its recent decision-making — an unusual and bold move of transparency in the middle of an active controversy. Paul Graham amplified this, praising the CEO's confidence in doing a real-time AMA on a sensitive topic at a politically charged moment.
